subject: chemistry
question_text: Using VSEPR theory, predict the shapes of the CO₂ and SO₂ molecules.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question comes from the enumeration sweep: the book teaches VSEPR only through NH₃ and H₂O inside its long answer and never asks a fresh predict-the-shape question, which is the standard examination use of the theory. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: CO₂
lines: CO₂: the central C atom has two bonding
regions (two double bonds) and NO lone
The two bonding regions move as far apart
steps.why: With no lone pair on carbon there is nothing to bend the molecule, so the two bonds settle exactly opposite each other.
common_mistakes: Counting a double bond as two separate repulsion regions. Each double bond acts as ONE region.
Drawing CO₂ bent like water. Carbon here has no lone pair.
steps.memory_tip: Two regions, no lone pair: a straight line.
steps.margin_note: State the pair count first; the shape follows from it.

steps.label: SO₂
lines: SO₂: the central S atom has two bonding
The lone pair occupies more space and
repels the bond pairs, reducing the angle
steps.why: The single lone pair is the whole difference between the two molecules: it pushes the two S−O bonds together, so SO₂ is bent while CO₂ stays linear.
common_mistakes: Writing SO₂ as linear by copying CO₂. Sulphur keeps one lone pair; carbon has none.
Giving the angle as exactly 120°. The lone pair reduces it slightly, to about 119°.
steps.memory_tip: Same formula shape, one lone pair different: CO₂ straight, SO₂ bent.
steps.margin_note: Box the two shapes together — the contrast is the answer.

insider_note: One mark per molecule, and the pair is set to catch a copied answer, because the lone pair on sulphur is the whole difference. State the region count for each first and both shapes follow from it.
